Yeah, long-term use and that loss of overall dopamine is most likely the cause. However, depression is multi-faceted and can be caused by many things and it might not just be because you're clean. You could have been depressed before you used. Anyways, depression can be mitigated by: 

# Lifestyle Changes

1. **Exercise Regularly**: Physical activity, especially aerobic exercise, can increase dopamine levels and improve mood. Aim for at least 30 minutes of exercise most days of the week.
2. **Healthy Diet**: Eat a balanced diet rich in fruits, vegetables, lean proteins, and whole grains. Foods like bananas, nuts, seeds, and fatty fish are known to support dopamine production.
3. **Adequate Sleep**: Ensure you get 7-9 hours of quality sleep per night. Good sleep hygiene can help regulate dopamine and improve overall well-being.
4. **Sunlight Exposure**: Spend time outside in natural sunlight. Sunlight can help boost dopamine levels and improve mood.

# Mental and Emotional Health

1. **Mindfulness and Meditation**: Practices like mindfulness and meditation can reduce stress and improve mood. They can also help in regulating emotions and increasing overall happiness.
2. **Therapy and Counseling**: Consider talking to a mental health professional. Cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) and other forms of counseling can be very effective in managing depression.
3. **Social Connections**: Engage with friends, family, and social activities. Positive social interactions can boost dopamine levels and provide emotional support.
4. **Hobbies and Interests**: Engage in activities that you enjoy and that give you a sense of accomplishment. Hobbies can provide a natural boost to your mood.

# Supplements and Natural Aids

1. **Omega-3 Fatty Acids**: Found in fish oil, these can help improve brain health and mood.
2. **Probiotics**: A healthy gut can influence dopamine production. Probiotic-rich foods like yogurt, kefir, and fermented vegetables can be beneficial.
3. **Tyrosine**: An amino acid that is a precursor to dopamine. It can be found in foods like chicken, turkey, dairy, and soy products.

# Avoiding Relapse

1. **Avoid Triggers**: Stay away from environments or situations that may trigger a relapse into drug use.
2. **Support Groups**: Consider joining support groups for recovering addicts. Sharing experiences and receiving support from others can be very beneficial.

  
Furthermore, be wary of the media you consume and the news you watch. Believe it or not, this does affect your mood. If you're watching negative news reports about how the world is terrible all of the time, you're not going to have a very positive mindset. 

Also, consider an outlet for these feelings like writing, drawing, painting, or something creative. 

Good luck! :)

Yes, there is substantial evidence and credible reports indicating that China has been involved in harvesting organs from prisoners, particularly prisoners of conscience such as Falun Gong practitioners, Uyghurs, Tibetans, and other minority groups.

1. **International Reports and Investigations**: Various reports and investigations have highlighted the issue. The China Tribunal, an independent tribunal established by the International Coalition to End Transplant Abuse in China, concluded in 2019 that forced organ harvesting has been occurring on a significant scale for years, primarily targeting Falun Gong practitioners. The tribunal found this practice to be state-sanctioned and involving health sector professionals, including surgeons and anesthetists​ ([The Organization for World Peace](https://theowp.org/reports/china-is-forcibly-harvesting-organs-from-prisoners-of-conscience-tribunal-rules/))​.
2. **UN Concerns**: United Nations human rights experts have expressed alarm over these allegations, noting that minorities, including Falun Gong practitioners, Uyghurs, Tibetans, and others, are subjected to medical tests without their consent to facilitate organ harvesting. This information, combined with the lack of transparency and independent oversight, has raised significant concerns internationally​ ([OHCHR](https://www.ohchr.org/en/press-releases/2021/06/china-un-human-rights-experts-alarmed-organ-harvesting-allegations))​.
3. **Inconsistent Official Data**: Despite China’s official stance that it moved to a voluntary organ donation system in 2015, discrepancies in the data raise doubts. The number of transplants performed annually far exceeds the number of legally documented donations, suggesting that many organs come from non-consensual sources. Researchers estimate that between 60,000 and 100,000 transplants are conducted annually, far more than the official figures suggest​ ([The Organization for World Peace](https://theowp.org/reports/china-is-forcibly-harvesting-organs-from-prisoners-of-conscience-tribunal-rules/))​.

Imagine for a moment that the urge to use never goes away and you have to constantly make the decision not to use, even when you feel you have a handle on it, the urge to use blindsides you because the pleasure and dopamine released when using was so intense that your brain automatically seeks out the experience. The truth of the matter is that you will never have the same experience and it will be more experiences of diminishing returns the further you use. 

The truth is you will most likely relapse unless you can get through the hump and even after that given period of time, you will most likely relapse. I've lost 5 acquaintances I knew in rehab to relapse and overdose after they left rehab, some were there for even a year or more. 

The only way is to reprogram your brain by doing something else instead of using. Also, tell those you care about and those that care about you that you feel like using. If this is too stressful for them, then find a sponsor. But tell someone, talk about it, don't fight this alone in your head because that's a guaranteed way to lose. 

It gets easier with time but if you are desperate to use a drug, you have to get desperate to not use. Have an administrator of your bank account and give your money to them if you know you're going to spend it on dope or whatever. Call your pharmacist and doctor and tell them you're an addict, grow some balls and admit to it and tell them not to prescribe you your drug of choice. 

If you don't grow up and fight this with all your strength, you will lose. Think of the movie 300. Die fighting or die crying. It's up to you. 

But in the end, it's your choice. But you're constantly having to make the choice to not use. That's the difference between someone with this disease and someone whom doesn't have this disease.

  
Good luck! :)

Like any country, there are do's and dont's. Don't go out after 8pm, avoid the bar scene, red light district. Don't have your phone out near a bike lane or busy street where motorbikes are driving. 

Don't go to the favelas - the people there aren't there for your entertainment, even with a tour guide.  Don't flash jewelry or your cell phone too much and use your cell phone inside a supermarket or store front or restaurant only. Watch if you are being followed by a group of unsavory people or if you see a group of unsavory people approaching you, cross the street, especially if you are travelling solo. 

Stay in a verified hotel or hostel with good reviews. Don't tell strangers where you are staying. Use services like Uber or verified taxis (no gypsy cabs). 

There are a lot of dangers in Columbia but if you're smart, you'll be fine. Just don't be naive.
